summary: Design and provision Slack channel deprecation workflow with automated Jira ticket creation and Confluence index update
description:
Issue summary: Request to build a managed deprecation workflow for Slack channels used across the org. Goal is to standardize how channels are flagged for deletion/archival, ensure owners are notified, create a Jira task for audit and approval, and automatically update the canonical Confluence channel index when archival completes.

Impact: Currently channel archival is ad-hoc and manual which leads to stale channels, missing owners, and noisy notifications. This workflow will reduce clutter, surface ownership gaps, and produce an auditable trail.

Request: 1) Add a Slack-native way (slash command and channel topic tag) for channel owners to mark channels for deprecation with a configurable TTL (14/30/90 days). 2) When a channel is marked, create a templated Jira task in project internal-support assigned to the channel owner with metadata (channel id, workspace, last active, member count). 3) Send an automated Slack modal to the channel owner that lists actions and requires confirmation; if owner unresponsive for a configured window, escalate to team admin. 4) After archival completes, update the Confluence channel index page to reflect status and attach the Jira ticket link and runbook snapshot. 5) Provide a dry-run mode and an audits-only mode for the first 60 days.

Acceptance criteria: - Slash command /deprecate-channel <ttl> creates a Jira issue with correct metadata and posts a confirmation message in the channel. - Owners receive modal and can confirm/extend/transfer ownership. - Unconfirmed deprecation escalates to the configured admin after X days. - Confluence index page is updated by automation after archival with ticket link. - Audit logs in the automation service show webhook events, Jira creation, and Confluence update.

Desired timeline: design + runbook 2 weeks, implementation + testing 3 weeks, pilot in #internal-tooling for 30 days, rollout org-wide after pilot.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) As a channel owner, run /deprecate-channel 30 in a test channel.
2) Expect immediate ephemeral confirmation message and Jira ticket created.
3) Open Jira ticket to verify template fields populated: channel_name, channel_id, owner, last_message_ts, member_count, suggested_archive_date.
4) Do not interact with modal; after escalation window verify admin gets notification.
5) When archival completed by bot, verify Confluence index row for channel shows status 'archived' and includes Jira ticket link.
investigation:
Preliminary notes: We already have bots that can create Jira tickets (see INT-645210) and a Confluence API integration. Major gaps: ownership resolution logic (Slack profile vs. team-admin mapping), escalation policy, and secure service account scope to write to Confluence. Need to validate rate limits for bulk updates to Confluence index and ensure the Jira project has a template scheme for these deprecation issues.
Potential approaches: leverage existing slack-app (channel-management-bot) and extend with a new endpoint that uses conn-service account with limited scopes; store TTL state in infra-config (DynamoDB) and schedule periodic reconciliation via GitHub Actions/runner or internal scheduler service.
Open questions: 1) Who is 'team admin' mapping source? 2) What is the escalation window default? 3) Are there legal retention exceptions for certain channels (legal/privacy)?

testing_notes: Dry-run mode: automation should log actions without mutating Jira/Confluence. Test steps: 1) enable dry-run via /deprecate-channel --dry-run. 2) Verify log entry includes payload sample and intended Jira payload. 3) Flatten to live mode and run on test channel. Edge-cases: channels without owners, private channels (needs explicit invite), channels with integrations (do not archive if active integrations unless owner confirms).
runbook_snippet: When a channel is marked for deprecation: 1) Bot captures channel metadata and creates INT-ticket auto-draft. 2) Send interactive modal to owner. 3) If confirmed-> schedule archival job at TTL expiry. 4) On archival-> post message to channel and update Confluence index row with link to ticket and archive timestamp. 5) If owner not found or flagged as 'legal-retain', mark ticket as 'needs manual review' and do not proceed.
notes_for_engineering: API footprints required: Slack chat:write, views.open, channels:read (or conversations:read), conversations:write for archiving; Jira: createIssue; Confluence: updateContent. Service account must be scoped to only the internal-support Jira project and the Confluence space used for the index. Include idempotency keys when creating Jira tickets to avoid duplicates. Add feature flag and pilot whitelist for #internal-tooling and #platform-oncall.
